title: Predicting the Premier League Season Through Data Science
summary: A 2026/27 Premier League forecast built from four player-value measures, five-season club history and three technically distinct 10,000-season simulation engines.
key_takeaway: Manchester City lead the calibrated consensus at 87.7 expected points, with Arsenal close behind at 85.5, but the margin between them is nowhere near as decisive as it looks. Confidence depends on both simulation variance within each engine and the visible distance among the three: some clubs agree across Foundations, Disruption and Momentum, others (like Bournemouth) see an eleven-point spread between engines that a single averaged forecast would hide entirely. The disagreement is the finding, not the noise around it.
